Alex —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. As promised, attaching a concise digest of our investigation, the verified timeline, and the concrete action sprint we will run with Heartwood over the next 30 days. Key points up front:

- Root cause (short): a cascading KV-cache eviction combined with an edge routing misconfiguration that caused higher-than-expected cold-starts for certain session patterns.
- Customer impact: intermittent tokenization latency spikes and session resets for ~2.5 hours on 2026-11-22 between 02:10–04:40 UTC, affecting ~12% of requests for the Heartwood production pool.
- Immediate remediation already applied: incremental cache tuning, deployment of guarded-prefetch to affected pool, and routing fix to prevent cross-region fallbacks.

What I'm sending now (attachments + links):
1) heartwood_evidence_bundle.zip — logs, sanitized request samples, kernel traces
2) rca-timeline.csv — minute-level timeline of events and operator actions
3) kv-cache-eviction-diagram.png — simplified diagram of the eviction sequence
4) Drive link: consolidated RCA doc with proposed rollout plan and test criteria

Action sprint (owners & deadlines):
- Week 1 (Nov 24–30): validation & guardrails — Hannah to deliver validation tests for patched pooling (deliverable: test matrix + pass/fail report).
- Week 2: broader rollout of guarded-prefetch + staged canaries (diego to coordinate with Heartwood ops).
- Week 3: monitoring and quality checks; if no regressions, finalize deployment.
- Week 4: run a joint load verification and sign-off call.

Please review the attached evidence and let me know any gaps you'd like us to fill. We propose the sign-off call on Dec 22, 2026 but are flexible.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
